title: Sparks of In Silico Cognitive Science: Theories from Simulated Data Can Generalize to Humans
abstract: arXiv:2609.08003v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Behavioral foundation models have been proposed as stand-ins for human participants across settings, but it is unclear whether theories discovered on them generalize to humans or merely characterize the simulator. We ran the Automated Cognitive Scientist (\textsc{AutoCog}), a closed-loop discovery system in which LLM agents design theory-discriminating experiments, collect responses, arbitrate between competing theories, and synthesize successors, entirely on behavior simulated by Centaur, a foundation model of human behavior. In a multi-attribute decision-making setting, the theories \textsc{AutoCog} found on Centaur generalized to human data: they outperformed canonical theories on ten held-out experiments and were rivaled only by theories found by running the same loop on people. We argue that this succeeds despite the simulator's inevitable imperfections because a discovery loop that arbitrates between competing theories demands less

translated_title: 计算机模拟认知科学的火花：从模拟数据中发现的理论能够泛化到人类
translated_abstract: 行为基础模型已被提议作为人类被试在各种场景中的替代品，但目前尚不清楚在其上发现的理论究竟是能够泛化到人类，还是仅仅刻画了模拟器本身。我们运行了自动化认知科学家系统（AutoCog），这是一个闭环发现系统，其中大语言模型智能体设计用于区分理论的实验、收集反应、在相互竞争的理论之间进行仲裁并合成后继理论——这一切完全基于由Centaur（一个人类行为基础模型）模拟的行为数据。在多属性决策场景中，AutoCog在Centaur上发现的理论成功泛化到了人类数据：它们在十项保留实验上超越了经典理论，且只有通过在真人身上运行相同循环所发现的理论才能与之相媲美。我们认为，尽管模拟器不可避免地存在缺陷，这一成功之所以能够实现，是因为在竞争理论之间进行仲裁的发现循环对模拟器的要求较低。
tldr: 在人类行为基础模型Centaur上，通过大语言模型驱动的自动化认知科学闭环系统发现的决策理论，能够成功泛化到真实人类数据并超越经典理论，证明基于模拟数据构建的心理学理论具有外部有效性。
en_tdlr: Theories discovered by an LLM-driven automated cognitive scientist running entirely on a simulated human behavioral foundation model (Centaur) generalize to real human data and outperform canonical theories, demonstrating that simulated-data-driven theory discovery can yield externally valid scientific insights about human cognition.
